title: Column fully braced at midheight by an elastic strut: critical load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.location: Example 9.8, part 1, sketch (a): plateau value; part 2 brace area
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. Units kip, in. Column ac of 2 x 13 ft, A = 7.08 in^2, I = 18.2 in^4, E = 29,000 ksi, base a pinned, top c held laterally, node b at midheight. Reference load 1 kip downward at c; the buckling factor is the critical load in kips. Linear buckling analysis. Horizontal strut bd at midheight, 10 ft long, A_br = 1.27 in^2 (the brace area of part 2, far above the 0.01136 in^2 the source derives as the minimum for buckling in two half waves), far end d held. Target: the plateau value 215.7 kips labelled on the source's plot (four-element model). The engine's members carry the exact stability functions (no discretisation error for a prismatic member with constant axial force); the source's computed values use a stated number of elements with a polynomial (approximate) geometric stiffness. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.

targets.precisionNote: printed "215.7"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; axis label of the source's plot; computed by the source with four elements and the polynomial geometric stiffness of its Eq. 9.14: an approximation by construction, no error bound stated
targets.sign: positive factor on a compressive load

quarantine.diagnosis: Source value is a discretised approximation; no stated error bound. Engine (exact stability functions): 214.05 kips = pi^2 EI/L^2 with L = 156 in (buckling in two half waves, as the source's text states for a sufficiently stiff brace); label on the source's plot 215.7 kips (four elements with the polynomial geometric stiffness of Eq. 9.14); difference 0.77 %, tolerance from the printed precision 2.3e-4. Evidence: a plane-frame calculation with the source's own element matrices gives 215.66 kips with four elements - the printed value - and 214.06 kips with sixteen. Buckling factors cannot be cross-checked by the foreign solvers of tier C.
